artists.biography: Martin Hannett (former North Manchester, Lancashire, England (31 May 1948 – 18 April 1991), sometimes credited as Martin Zero, was a record producer who helped develop Joy Division and was an original partner in Factory Records with Tony Wilson. Hannett's trademark sound, most apparent on Joy Division's debut album Unknown Pleasures and its follow-up, Closer, is sparse and eerie, complementing frontman Ian Curtis' baritone vocals. For complete Wiki, go here: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Hannett Read more on Last.fm. User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.

perplexity.description:
Hannett's Electronic Recordings - Homage To Delia Derbyshire, released in 2017 by Martin Hannett on Ozit-Morpheus Records, is a collection of experimental electronic music inspired by the pioneering work of Delia Derbyshire. The album features 18 tracks sourced from sessions at Strawberry Studios in Stockport, showcasing Hannett’s innovative use of tape loops, synthesizers, and studio manipulation. Musically, the record sits firmly within the realm of early British electronic experimentation, echoing the avant-garde spirit of Derbyshire’s own compositions while reflecting Hannett’s signature production techniques.

As a posthumous release, the album stands as a unique entry in Hannett’s discography, which is best known for his influential production work with post-punk bands like Joy Division and Buzzcocks. Unlike his more commercially recognized productions, this album highlights his lesser-known but significant contributions to electronic music, revealing a deep engagement with the genre’s formative years. The limited vinyl pressing of 300 copies and its release through Ozit Dandelion underscore its status as a cult artifact rather than a mainstream offering.

Critically, the album was received as an important archival discovery, praised for its historical value and its homage to Derbyshire’s legacy. Reviewers noted its atmospheric textures and the way it bridges the gap between early electronic experimentation and later developments in ambient and industrial music. While not a commercial blockbuster, Homage To Delia Derbyshire has been recognized as a significant release for fans of electronic music history and for those interested in the roots of British avant-garde sound.
